study type: In vitro experimental study and comparative tissue analysis
cohort: Primary cervical smooth muscle cells (CSMC) from pregnant women and cervical tissue from non-pregnant women, all categorized with or without premature cervical failure (PCF).
finding: Having soft cervical ECM, characterized by decreased collagen cross-link maturity ratios in women with PCF, may lead to decreased CSMC contractile tone and a predisposition to sphincter laxity that contributes to spontaneous preterm birth.
mod_finding: The study suggests that a predisposition to sphincter laxity, caused by soft cervical ECM and decreased CSMC contractile tone, contributes to premature cervical softening/dilation necessary for preterm vaginal delivery.
cross-section timing: Samples were taken from pregnant women and non-pregnant women; specific timing within pregnancy or post-delivery for non-pregnant women is not specified.
